newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Saab Aircraft data still negative.
newsitem.headline: Saab Aircraft data still negative.

text.p: Saab Aircraft, a division of Saab AB which is wholly owned by Investor AB, on Monday said income from manufacturing the Saab 340 and Saab 2000 planes continued to be negative.
Saab reported civilian aircraft sales worth 2.08 billion crowns ($314 million) in the nine months ended September 30 compared with 1.77 billion a year earlier but put no figure on the net loss.
"Competition from recently established jet programmes is very severe in the 50 passenger segment where Saab 2000 is sold," Saab said in a statement.
By September, Saab Military Aircraft had delivered 27 of 30 JAS 39 Gripen aircraft ordered by the Swedish Air Force.
The order backlog includes a further 110 planes and on December 13, the Swedish parliament will decide whether to authorise further orders.
Saab AB, which also includes dynamics, training systems and combitech divisions, reported a fall in profit after financial income and expenses to 84 million crowns from 223 million.
The group's new orders for the first nine months were 5.69 million crowns compared with 4.2 billion, and the order backlog at the end of September was 20.54 billion crowns against 21.29 billion.
Saab Automobile AB, jointly owned by Investor and General Motors Corp, did not report nine-month figures.
